video.title: Forget Big Apps. These Tiny Tools Are Making Millions

summary: Chris Koerner explains 'the great unbundling': as Craigslist was split into billion-dollar companies, platforms like Apify, Clay, Zapier and OpenAI can be split into single-purpose tools. He profiles Nico, a former pasta maker turned SDR who vibe-coded a Google Maps lead scraper on an Apify actor. It charges $35/month convertible into credits and reached $3,500 MRR in about 7 months with near-zero costs and word-of-mouth growth. Chris then lists 12+ ideas built the same way, including niche scrapers, Amazon review reports, a Zapier support bot, a micro-influencer finder, an Upwork search tool, a single-feature Clay, a niche 'Zillow' for RV parks or laundromats, and a Shopify-only BuiltWith. His advice is to move fast before the window closes.

tactics.name: API arbitrage build
steps: Pick an Apify actor (or Clay/Zapier feature)
Copy its API key
Vibe-code a simple site with a search bar in Replit/Lovable/Codex/Claude
Add Stripe
Buy a ~$10 domain
Charge a markup per result or subscription

quote.text: You're just putting a simple storefront on top of someone else's software
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Subscription-to-credits pricing
steps: Charge monthly
Convert unused spend into non-expiring credits
Let cancelled users return and use credits

quote.text: if they canceled their account, they could still come back 9 months later and use the rest of their credits
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Shopify list cross-sell
steps: Get a list of all Shopify stores (BuiltWith or an Upwork VA)
Sell 10-20 different tools to the same list
See which resonates

tactics.name: Find hot business categories on BizBuySell
steps: Scrape all Texas listings
Scrape again a week later and subtract what sold
Repeat weekly for a month
Build niche marketplaces for fastest-selling categories

quote.text: scrape everything in Texas on Bisby by sell again and then subtract what sold

tactics.name: Ad-test multiple micro-SaaS ideas
steps: Build five ideas
Spend $100 ads on each
Keep the one with lowest CPA

steps: Pick something to unbundle

lessons.lesson: Big platforms bundle thousands of features; unbundling one into a focused product for a niche is the opportunity.
Customers assume a single-purpose tool is better and will pay more for an easier UI.

quote.text: If you're only scraping one thing, then the customer assumes you're better at it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pricing that respects usage patterns (rollover credits) beats subscription fatigue.
Non-technical founders can ship with AI coding tools plus a technical friend for fixes.
'A feature can be a company' is now true; build lifestyle businesses.

quote.text: The phrase nothing is too niche has never been more true. A feature can be a company
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: One customer list (e.g. Shopify stores) can be sold many different tools.
Design quality matters; ugly niche sites are vulnerable to well-designed competitors.
Self-serve tools can run with near-zero support and grow via word of mouth.

evidence_quality.rationale: Nico's numbers are second-hand from Chris; most ideas are untested hypotheticals.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor read for .online domains; promotes PlayMakers AI (Chris's company).
